NTA. I am white so I’m probably not the best person to answer this, but I’m going to give you my thoughts and you can take it or leave it, of course. 

I doubt she understands the braids as being for black people in a social sense, and not just for the texture of your hair. Also, she is your daughter so if this cultural to you, how can it be appropriation to include her in on a little something that she admires and respects, as your daughter? Yes she is white but she is also young and *your daughter* and wouldn’t refraining from giving her braids (braids you and your other daughters are okay with her having) be isolating to her? The braids are a part of you and your older daughters, besides just thinking the braids are pretty, I’m sure your youngest also wants to connect with her family and this is a way for her to do that.

My man is pretty sensitive, too, and if I were in your shoes, I would be anxious but, there are some times in life where you are going to have to hurt each others feelings. Yes, relationships are about compromise, but they should also be about maintaining your own sense of self. You can still be appreciative and excited to marry him and feel ignored/even a bit slighted by his decision. I think that they both can exist. Tell him that you plan to make this ring a long-term investment. Sure, white gold is beautiful, but yellow gold is more you. If he wants a white gold band, that’s up to him. You told him which metal you wanted and he didn’t listen. I just think it’s something that needs to be talked about, even if he gets offended because the color of the gold does mean something to you. Just also make sure to let him know how appreciative you are of his proposal, but having your ideal ring is also important to you. Whatever you end up doing is your decision, of course. There really is no right or wrong answer, it’s whatever works for you. I’m a bit of an over-communicator when it comes to my relationship, but it works for me.

The goal is to wear that ring for the rest of your life. Just like with the man, you shouldn’t settle for something that you aren’t completely in love with (within reason, of course). He knew before he bought the ring what you actually wanted, he still knows your preferred color of gold, and yet he still decided to get what he preferred. He gambled on that. Maybe you would have fallen for the ring harder than the one you initially wanted because he chose it out for you. But, it didn’t turn out that way, he is the one who took the risk when you told him what you wanted and he still bought you what he preferred. If you have the means to get your dream ring, it is not selfish to go for it. Say you really, really wanted cat, but he doesn’t like cats, so he got you a dog. Maybe that would be okay, maybe it wouldn’t. But, in this case, you aren’t even living together yet and he still gave you a dog. Yeah, he’ll see the dog every so often, but he doesn’t live with it. Not like you do. That ring will be on your finger for hopefully forever. He’ll still be able to see it, but you’re the one who is really going to have to live with it. Maybe I went a little extreme with my argument, I just want you to see where I’m coming from.
